reasoning: The icon clearly depicts a computer keyboard crossed out with a diagonal slash, indicating a disabled, disconnected, hidden, or broken keyboard. While originally a UI glyph for hiding an on-screen keyboard, it fits a real niche of tasks around troubleshooting unresponsive keyboards, disabling built-in laptop keys, suppressing virtual keyboards in software development, or taking no-typing ergonomic breaks. It should not be used for general keyboard tasks (buying, cleaning, typing), which belong to the unslashed keyboard icon.
